projectDescription: A PHP extension that runs untrusted JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, or PHP inside PHP — sandboxed in WebAssembly — against a typed capability SDK you define in plain PHP.
keyFeatures: Language-agnostic guest execution — JavaScript (QuickJS-ng or Boa), TypeScript, Python (RustPython), or PHP all run from a single uniform API; swap the .wasm to change languages
In-process WebAssembly isolation boundary — a bug in the guest's own language engine cannot reach the PHP host, with no outer container or microVM required
Typed capability allowlist — you register plain PHP functions; the guest sees only those names, nothing else, via a flat dispatch table that is the entire trust boundary
TypeScript checked inside the sandbox — the real tsc runs in the guest and type-checks every eval against a .d.ts generated from your registered PHP SDK before execution
Automatic SDK type inference — PHP function signatures and PHPDoc (including nested array{} shapes) are reflected into .d.ts, .pyi, and .php stubs for guest authors
Bounded and optionally deterministic execution — memory, wall-clock (epoch), stack, and fuel limits; fuel gives reproducible runs
Synchronous-only mode — syncOnly: true makes the TypeScript guest reject async/await/generators and every use of a Promise at compile time
Type-argument schema extraction — analyze() derives JSON Schema from a TypeScript call's type argument and returns canonical, hashable bytes keyed by ordinal
Ahead-of-time precompilation — Terrarium::precompile() moves Cranelift compilation into the build pipeline for cold-start-free deployments (AWS Lambda/Bref ready)
Capability handles for live objects — grant()/resolve()/revoke() pass opaque integer handles to the guest for DB connections, file handles, and other stateful resources
publicApiSurface: Terrarium\Runtime (engine primitive — direct access, accepts bytes instead of paths, setCompileOptions/setTypes)
Terrarium\GuestException (guest program error — type + message + line)
Terrarium\TrapException (WASM trap: unreachable, OOB, bad indirect call)
